record.original_question: Let M be a compact 4-manifold with boundary homeomorphic to a connected sum #m(S1 ⊗ S2), with m > 0, and let Mbar be the associated closed 4-manifold obtained by attaching the corresponding 4-dimensional handlebody. Theorem 13 states that if M admits a gem-induced trisection, then Mbar admits a trisection with the same central surface and therefore gT(Mbar) <= gGT(M). Under what conditions on a gem of M does equality hold, so that the trisection genus of Mbar is exactly the G-trisection genus of M?

evidence.quote: Theorem 13 ([11]) Let M be a compact 4-manifold with boundary ∂M ∼= #m(S1 ⊗S2), with m > 0. If M admits a gem-induced trisection, then Mbar ∼= M ∪ Y^(~)_m admits a trisection with the same central surface. As a consequence, gT(Mbar) ≤ gGT(M).
On the other hand, it would also be interesting to investigate conditions on the gems of a compact 4-manifold, so that in Theorem 13 the equality holds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A trisection of a closed, connected, orientable 4-manifold X is a decomposition X = X_1 ∪ X_2 ∪ X_3 in which each X_i is diffeomorphic to a 4-dimensional handlebody ♮^{k_i}(S^1 × B^3), each pairwise intersection X_i ∩ X_j is a 3-dimensional handlebody, and the triple intersection Σ = X_1 ∩ X_2 ∩ X_3 is a closed orientable surface (the central surface). The trisection genus gT(X) is the minimum genus of Σ over all trisections of X.

For a compact, connected, orientable 4-manifold M with boundary ∂M ≅ #_m(S^1 × S^2) (m > 0), let Y_m = ♮^m(S^1 × B^3) denote the standard 4-dimensional handlebody bounded by #_m(S^1 × S^2), and let M̄ = M ∪_{∂M} Y_m be the closed 4-manifold obtained by capping off.

An (edge-coloured) gem of M is a regular 5-coloured graph encoding a coloured triangulation of M; a gem of M is said to induce a (generalized, or G-) trisection of M when its colour structure produces a decomposition of M into three pieces with central surface Σ, analogous to the closed case but adapted to the boundary. The G-trisection genus gGT(M) is the minimum genus of the central surface over all gem-induced G-trisections of M.

It is known that whenever M admits a gem-induced G-trisection of central genus g, M̄ inherits a trisection with the same central surface, so that
   gT(M̄) ≤ gGT(M).

Problem. Determine necessary and sufficient combinatorial conditions on a gem (5-coloured graph) of such a compact 4-manifold M with boundary #_m(S^1 × S^2) under which the induced inequality is sharp, i.e. under which
   gT(M̄) = gGT(M).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit direction for further investigation regarding when equality holds in the inequality gT(M̄) ≤ gGT(M) arising from gem-induced trisections. No published resolution was located; the problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: Gem-induced trisections of compact PL 4-manifolds (arXiv:2502.01757)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Theorem 13 relating gGT(M) and gT(M̄) and lists investigating equality conditions as an open direction.
status_evidence.claim: The equality case is posed as an open problem.
